subject: Clarify: Helio Health redlines re: output ownership & model training
messages:
From: Emily Park <emily.park@heliohealth.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@heliohealth.com
Date: 2026-11-20 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Redlines: MSA + Order Form - output ownership & training

Hi Michael,

Thanks for the MSA and order form — attached are Helio's redlines (see Helio_Redlines_20261120.pdf). The primary open items for legal are:

- Output ownership: We need explicit language that Helio owns outputs generated by the service when the prompt/data is provided by Helio or its end users.
- Model training & derived models: Helio will not permit Redwood to use Helio-provided content or Helio-generated outputs to train, fine-tune, or improve models unless Helio provides an explicit, written opt-in.
- Feedback/telemetry: We can accept submission of anonymized telemetry for service quality, but only aggregated metrics and no retention of item-level user content for model training.

Please confirm that Redwood can accept these carveouts and provide suggested contract language (MSA and order form) that we can review. Procurement would like a written response and the revised documents by Monday EOD PT so we can keep the deal on the approval timeline.

Thanks,
Emily Park
Senior Counsel, Legal Operations
Helio Health

Attachments: Helio_Redlines_20261120.pdf (redline copy of MSA + Order Form)

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Emily Park <emily.park@heliohealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-20 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redlines: MSA + Order Form - output ownership & training

Emily — thanks for the clear redlines and the timeline. I looped in Laura (legal) and Karthik (product/serving) to draft contract language and confirm product constraints. High-level response up front:

- Output ownership: We can accept a forward-looking clause clarifying that customer-generated prompts and outputs are the customer's content and that Redwood will not assert ownership. We typically retain narrow rights to operate and to provide the service.
- Model training: Redwood's policy is that we do not use customer-provided content or generated outputs to train our base models without an opt-in. We can add explicit order form language confirming no training without opt-in.
- Feedback/telemetry: We can offer an explicit limited "service improvement" license that is scoped to aggregated, de-identified telemetry and excludes item-level retention for model training.

Action items for internal follow-up: Laura, please draft MSA and order form language that: (a) adds a clear customer output ownership paragraph; (b) adds an explicit "no training without opt-in" clause; and (c) defines a limited feedback license that permits only aggregated, de-identified telemetry for service maintenance and safety. Karthik, can you confirm product feasibility for locking telemetry pipelines so that we can guarantee no item-level retention for training?

We will aim to return a redlined response by Monday EOD PT. If Helio prefers, we can do a 30-min call to walk through the language.

Best,
Michael Grant
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

--
Replying on behalf of Redwood. Internal recipients looped for legal and product input.

From: procurement@heliohealth.com

Michael,

Thanks for the quick reply. Procurement needs two things to proceed with legal routing:

1) A short written confirmatory clause for the order form that states: 'Redwood will not use Customer-provided data or Customer-generated outputs to train models or improve model weights without Customer's prior written consent.'
2) SOC 2 Type II evidence (or SOC 2 report link) and a short note on data retention policies for telemetry used for product improvement.

If you can put both in the Monday response that Emily requested, we can advance the internal approval.

Regards,
Helio Procurement

Attachment: Helio_Procurement_Checklist.xlsx (see items 3 and 7)

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Emily Park <emily.park@heliohealth.com>, procurement@heliohealth.com
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-22 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redlines: MSA + Order Form - output ownership & training (Redwood response attached)

Team — attaching Redwood_response_redlines_20261122.docx that contains redline proposals and suggested language. Summary of the commitments in the draft: 

- Customer Output Ownership: Clause added to MSA Sec. 4.1 and mirrored in Order Form: 'Customer retains ownership of Customer Content and any Outputs generated from Customer Content; Redwood shall have no ownership or title to such Outputs.'
- No Training Without Opt-in: Order Form appendix language: 'Redwood will not use Customer Content or Outputs to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve Redwood models destined for general use without Customer's prior written opt-in. Customer may elect to opt into a Productized Training Program under separate terms.'
- Limited Feedback License (Telemetry): We propose a narrow license limited to aggregated, de-identified telemetry for safety, debugging, and service-quality improvements only. Item-level content will not be retained in the training corpus. The draft is intentionally prescriptive on retention windows and access controls.

Next steps / asks: 
- Laura: please review and tidy the redline language for legal sign-off.
- Karthik: confirm we can implement a telemetry pipeline with guaranteed item-level expunge and a documented retention window (we propose 30 days for item-level telemetry, then aggregated retention thereafter).
- Emily / Procurement: confirm whether the proposed language addresses Helio's requirement; if yes, we will prepare DocuSign-ready MSA + Order Form.

Thanks — I appreciate the quick turnaround.

Regards,
Michael Grant
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_response_redlines_20261122.docx (Redwood redline + commentary)
